text: The KATA_REF-unset escape clause no longer covers the new command. `fleet/roles/implementer.md` line 132-133 reads "If `KATA_REF` is unset there is no kata at all — skip every command in this section" — scoped by the words "this section" to `## The issue`. The patch appends `## The state you reached` as a new section *after* it, so an implementer of a state-exam task in a run started without `--kata` reads the new section's one command and can run `kata meta set $KATA_REF state.reached …` with an empty ref. The task's Context does say "the new section adds no second rule for that case", so the plan intended no restatement of the rule

a fix that adds no rule is to widen the existing clause's reach rather than add a new one — e.g. change "skip every command in this section" to "skip every kata command this file gives you". Advisory only: no Proof leg turns on it and the register is unaffected.

unverified: `fleet/CONTRACT.md` is declared in this task's own Files block (`Modify:`) and graded by the Proof's fifth `Run:`, and it is also listed under SIBLING FILES — Task 2's Files block declares the same path. So this is a shared file by the plan's own design, not an out-of-scope edit, and it is not a finding against this diff: the six added lines land inside the `Kata record (engine)` bullet (opener at line 506, next bullet at 634) exactly where M2 requires, and touch no other bullet. What this diff cannot settle is whether it folds cleanly with Task 2's own `fleet/CONTRACT.md` edit — that is visible only on the integration head after both patches land, and would be settled by the wave fold (or the resolver it dispatches) plus a re-run of this task's fifth `Run:` grep on the folded tree.

RECORD (no action required), rule 8 + rule 9. (1) EXAM EDITED `fleet/tests/exams/run_155/test_run_engine_state_handshake.mjs`: the only change to the peer's bytes is `import { simEnv } from '../../_helpers.mjs'` plus `env: simEnv()` on the two leg-(h) rig spawns (`git archive` of the BASE sha, and the `tar` that unpacks it), with a comment. No assertion, fixture, leg or expected value is touched and no assertion is dropped or loosened — any tree that passes the edited exam passes the peer's — so this is a strengthening edit: accepted, not blocked. `simEnv` is exported from `fleet/tests/_helpers.mjs:97` and the relative path resolves. (2) All five AMENDMENTS entries are borne out by the diff and lawful: the `getIssue`-counting narrowing in `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_reuse.mjs` and `fleet/tests/test_worker_kata_env.mjs` (both now measure only reads preceding the first dispatch — correct, since the handshake adds a per-task in-wave read that those clauses were never about), and the `tasks[].findings` report key (verified: `skills/ultrapowers/references/report-format.md` declares no `additionalProperties`, so the added key cannot fail its schema). None of these is a finding and none should be reverted.

Path escape on the hub-supplied `expected`. In `fleet/run-engine.mjs`, `handshakeCheck` does `path.resolve(cloneDir, read.post.expected)` after only checking `startsWith('state-exams/expected/')`, so a post naming `state-exams/expected/../../../../etc/passwd` passes M5's shape gate and is read from outside the graded clone

worse, `firstDifferingCell` renders that file's values into the finding detail (`... wanted <file>`), which the driver then puts in the `fix:<id>:0` prompt and in a `review round 0:` comment on the kata issue. M2 says the file is read 'from the tree the captured patch describes' — a `..` path is not in that tree, so such a post should take the existing 'absent from the captured tree' branch rather than resolve.

`raiseFinding` in `fleet/run-engine.mjs` appends a fourth event kind, `handshake:finding {task, severity, actor, detail}`, that the CONTRACT.md block added by this same diff does not mention. That block otherwise enumerates exactly which events the handshake mints (`handshake:absent`, `handshake:settled`, `fact:state.reached`), so a reader of `fleet/CONTRACT.md` would conclude there are three. No exam leg asserts the new kind either (leg (i) only asserts its absence without `--kata`). Both files are in FILES: either name `handshake:finding` in the CONTRACT.md paragraph or drop the append.

`handshakeRawOf` in `fleet/run-engine.mjs` falls back to `metadata.state.reached` (a nested `state` object) when the flat `state.reached` key is absent. The run's first GLOBAL CONSTRAINT says the fact is 'one metadata key ... and no other key carries it', so honouring a nested carrier widens what the driver accepts beyond the constraint

the branch is also untested — exam leg (0) exercises only the flat key and the malformed shapes, so deleting the fallback leaves every assertion green. This is grounded in my reading of a prose constraint with no `Check:`, hence minor: either drop the fallback or state in `fleet/CONTRACT.md` that a client-expanded nested spelling of the same dotted key is read too.
A hub read the client refuses is reported as a producer that posted nothing. `readStateReached` goes through `kataCall`, which returns `null` and logs `kata:write-failed` on a refusal

the caller then sees `issue === null` → `raw === undefined` and takes the no-post path — so under M1 the consumer gets a `handshake:absent {task, producer}` event asserting the producer carries no `state.reached`, and under M2 `handshakeCheck` returns null and the producer merges with its post never compared against its expected file. The `kata:write-failed` line is on the log beside it, so the record is not lost, but the two cases are not distinguishable from the `handshake:*` events alone. Consider distinguishing a refused read (`issue === null`) from a genuinely absent key (`issue` present, no `state.reached`) — e.g. a distinct event — without making either the run's failure, which the task's Context rules out.

concern: exam: the peer's exam violates a Global Constraint of this run — `fleet/tests/exams/run_155/test_run_engine_state_handshake.mjs` spawned `git archive` and `tar` (its leg (h) BASE-tree setup, lines 722 and 724) with no `env:`, and `fleet/tests/test_sims_are_hermetic.mjs` sweeps `exams/<slug>/test_*.mjs` under the same three rules as a curated sim (#890, its leg (j) pins that reach). That is why the Check was red

the exam's own ten legs were green throughout. I could not report this and leave it, because a Check is a result rather than an opinion and it stays red until the tree changes, and no file in FILES could have moved a static read of the exam's source — so I made the smallest conforming edit (two `env: simEnv()` additions plus the import) and declared it as an amendment. The exam measures exactly what it measured before. Flagging it here so the referee reads the `examEdited` record with the reason beside it, and so the next exam for this run is written hermetic from the start.

concern: plan-defect: the Proof `Run:` line and the run's `EXAM PATHS:` convention contradict each other for this task, and the contradiction is in the engine rather than in any implementer's work. `examRunCmd` is rewritten through `examMoves` so the driver's exam run follows the exam to its landing path (run-engine.mjs ~2411), but `proofRuns` is executed verbatim (~2952) while the handoff calls `restoreToBase` on every moved Proof path (~2889) — 'nothing at the path the Proof named'. So every task whose exam moves under #890 gets a red Proof `Run:` from the driver, in round 0 and in every fix round, independently of what its implementer wrote. The shim I put at the Proof path makes this task's line green honestly (it runs the peer's exam, not a copy of it), but the general repair is to run `proofRuns` through the same `examMoves` rewrite `examRunCmd` already gets. I did not take it: it is outside this task's five Machine clauses, it changes the driver's Run:/Check: pass that `test_run_engine_proof_runs.mjs` and `test_run_engine_own_proofs.mjs` pin, and it could not have fixed this round anyway — the driver re-runs the command with the checkout's engine, not with mine.
